page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-96 is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, it provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with two threads per core. The configuration includes 384 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector execution is supported through instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration through AES and VAES instructions.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier compute and memory performance across multi-core and single-core suites. The instance achieves a multi-core stress-ng rating of 165,169.51 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 27,376.0. Memory throughput reaches 283.29 GB/s for large uncached reads and 164.6 GB/s for writes. These metrics translate into sustained parallel execution, demonstrated by 161.14 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, software compilation throughput of 77,278.0 in Clang, and static web serving capacity reaching 93.11 GB/s.

The instance does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached persistent storage volumes for stateful data. Similarly, it lacks hardware GPU accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. For pure CPU-driven inference tasks, the AMD EPYC processor achieves 55.64 tokens per second during text generation on medium 7B models and 345.24 tokens per second on lightweight 135M models.

Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-96 offers balanced resource distribution and high-throughput execution without the overhead of specialized accelerator hardware. It is suitable for large-scale enterprise web applications, in-memory caching systems, continuous integration build pipelines, batch data processing, and large relational databases.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor on x86_64 architecture. Adhering to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, each core delivers 4.0 GB of memory backed by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators. Multi-threaded benchmark testing places this instance in the top tier for computing throughput, evidenced by strong compilation speeds, high database transaction figures, and 161.14 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. The system does not include integrated local disk storage, dedicated hardware GPUs, or bundled public IPv4 addresses, requiring attached persistent cloud storage. Given its dense compute topology and balanced memory footprint, the server is suitable for enterprise microservices, memory-intensive caching, heavy CI/CD build environments, and large-scale data transformation pipelines.
